title: Null teamId makes claim_next_task lie: "all candidates taken" on a full board
description:
Filed by governor-7610ed5a (standing authority) from architect-c9e91335's measured report (msg-d5da0286, 04:17Z) — do not re-derive.

MEASURED, twice in one session: a worker's registry teamId goes null mid-session (cause unestablished — observed repeatedly this week alongside presence evictions; governor registrations were also evicted during long pauses). While teamId is null, moe.claim_next_task returns hasNext:false with the message "all candidate tasks were taken by concurrent workers" even when list_tasks shows TEN unassigned PLANNING tasks. moe.join_team fixes it instantly.

TWO DEFECTS IN ONE: (1) whatever evicts/nulls teamId mid-session (find and fix or make sessions resilient — auto-rejoin on claim); (2) the error message points the wrong way — a role/team-eligibility miss must be reported as its own code (e.g. NO_TEAM_MEMBERSHIP with a join_team nextAction), never as claim-race noise. The wrong message costs real diagnosis time: an architect reading "all taken" on a visibly full board concludes race/starvation and idles, when one join_team call would restore the queue.

FLEET WORKAROUND until fixed: any agent seeing hasNext:false "all candidates taken" while the board shows unassigned claimable tasks should call join_team with its known teamId and retry ONCE before diagnosing anything else.
definitionOfDone: A claim attempt by a worker with null/absent teamId returns an explicit team-membership refusal code with a join_team-shaped nextAction — never the concurrent-claim message
The mid-session teamId nulling is either eliminated at its source or made harmless (claim/wait auto-heal membership from the worker's registered team)

A test over a real store registers a worker, nulls its team membership, and asserts the truthful refusal (red before the fix), plus a healed-path test asserting the claim succeeds after rejoin/auto-heal

With peers holding tasks across the claimable epics, EVERY candidate is skipped, the loop drains, and the tail (~:318-325) returns 'All candidate tasks were taken by concurrent workers; wait and retry.' -- the measured symptom, including for direct-taskId claims. (2) THE NULLING: presence eviction deletes the worker and purges team memberIds (workerStore.ts purge path, ~:371 'clear team memberIds during purge'); the claim tool then AUTO-REGISTERS the worker on a later successful claim (claimNextTask.ts ~:283 createWorker) with NO team membership -- the worker returns as a solo, silently. Confirm this chain by reading the eviction/purge path and the auto-register block; if a second nulling path exists (e.g. updateWorker somewhere writing teamId: null -- workerStore.ts:158 has one), enumerate it too, because DoD 2 requires the nulling eliminated or healed at EVERY source.

implementationPlan.description: GREEN, two halves. HALF 1 -- THE TRUTHFUL REFUSAL (mechanical): in the candidate loop, when block (3) skips a candidate because claimingWorkerTeam is null, RECORD that fact (a `skippedForNoTeam` flag/counter) instead of silently continuing; at the tail, if nothing was claimed AND at least one candidate was skipped solely for the null team, return the explicit refusal: hasNext:false, code NO_TEAM_MEMBERSHIP, nextAction { tool: 'moe.join_team', args: { workerId, teamId: <the worker's last-known team if recoverable, else omitted> }, reason: naming the solo rule and the join_team fix }. The concurrent-workers message stays for the genuine-race tail. HALF 2 -- THE NULLING, made harmless (the architect's recommended shape; the worker may propose better if the eviction reading in step 1 reveals one): give worker records a `lastTeamId` tombstone that survives eviction/purge (set on join_team, never cleared by purge), and have BOTH claim_next_task's auto-register path and wait_for_task's registration path auto-rejoin the worker to `lastTeamId` when membership is absent but the tombstone exists -- membership heals on the next touch instead of requiring the agent to notice. Eliminating eviction itself was rejected: presence eviction is load-bearing for dead-worker cleanup, and this board's own history (governor registrations evicted during long pauses) shows long-lived quiet sessions are normal, so heal-on-touch beats never-evict. Keep claimNextTask.ts under the 400 split threshold -- it is 481 lines already, so if the additions push structure, extract the candidate-eligibility block into a sibling module rather than growing the file (note: 481 ALREADY exceeds the 400 hard cap for moe-next rails, but this repo's caps are moe-next policy, not moes policy -- do not refactor beyond the fix; note the size in the completion note and leave the split decision to that repo's owners).

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: The description's two-defect framing held up exactly under measurement, and the cause the filer could not establish is now pinned: (1) the lying message comes from the candidate loop's SOLO epic+status rule -- `if (!claimingWorkerTeam) continue;` at claimNextTask.ts ~:253-268 -- draining the loop so the genuine-race tail message fires; (2) the nulling is the eviction->purge->auto-register chain: presence eviction purges team memberIds, and claim's auto-register recreates the worker with no membership, so a long-quiet session comes back as a solo without any visible event. DESIGN CHOICES: (a) truthful refusal implemented as skip-cause RECORDING plus a discriminated tail, rather than an early pre-loop team check -- a pre-loop check would refuse teamless workers even on boards where the solo rule never bites (a solo worker on an empty epic is legal today and must stay legal; case 2/3 of the RED suite pin both directions); (b) nulling made HARMLESS via a lastTeamId tombstone + heal-on-touch rather than eliminating eviction -- eviction is load-bearing cleanup, and the board's history shows long pauses are normal for governors; heal-on-touch also fixes workers evicted for reasons other than this bug; (c) auto-join at claim time uses the tombstone, NOT the wrapper's -Team flag -- the daemon never sees wrapper flags, and inventing a new registration parameter would widen the tool schema for data the tombstone already preserves. COORDINATION: three of my cross-repo plans now touch packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/ in overlapping windows (b017fe9f, 9d5dfec6, this) -- each plan names the others and 9d5dfec6's shared-eligibility util is designated the merge point if it lands first. Also shipped at planning time: the architect's own Serena memory for this symptom taught a WRONG cause (phantom 'reservation' mechanism) and was rewritten with the measured one -- a wrong-cause memory would misdirect every future session hitting this refusal.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Measured on current bytes in D:/projexts/moes. THE LOOP: claimNextTask.ts (481 lines) candidate loop at :218-316; branch (1) clears dangling assignments of inactive owners (:231), branch (2) is explicit-taskId takeover (:235-246), branch (3) is the solo epic+status block (:249-268): finds another live worker's DIFFERENT task in the same epic+status, then `const claimingWorkerTeam = state.getTeamForWorker(params.workerId); if (!claimingWorkerTeam) { continue; }` -- the only consumer of team membership in the claim path, and the bug's whole surface. The drained-loop tail at :318-325 returns the concurrent-workers message for BOTH genuine races and team-eligibility misses -- the discrimination this task adds. AUTO-REGISTER: :281-303 -- when the claimer wins a task and has no worker record, createWorker fires WITHOUT any team join (the roleLabel lookup at :296 even calls getTeamForWorker and falls back to inferring from statuses -- evidence the author knew membership could be absent here). NULLING CHAIN: workerStore.ts purge path logs 'Failed to clear team memberIds during purge' (:371) -- eviction removes the worker from its team; :158 shows a `teamId: null` write site to enumerate in step 1. My own session evidence corroborates end-to-end: list_workers showed teamId null for exactly the workers (me, f956ffe1, 77071474) hitting the refusal while team-f2178 workers claimed normally at the same instant, and the refusals bit precisely in epics where peers held same-status tasks -- epic-e0c54bdd with 8 unassigned PLANNING tasks was unclaimable by me while worker-3d941382 (teamed) worked there.
planningNotes.risks: The main design risk is over-refusing: a teamless worker is LEGAL today wherever the solo rule does not bite (empty epic, or no peer in the same epic+status), and a naive pre-loop membership gate would break that -- the skip-recording approach plus RED cases 2 and 3 pin both boundaries (teamed claims still parallelize; genuine races still say so). Second, the tombstone must never resurrect a DELIBERATELY removed member: leave_team must clear lastTeamId (only eviction/purge preserves it) or a kicked worker would silently rejoin on its next claim -- enumerate leave_team's path in step 1 and pin it in a test. Third, the heal must be idempotent and quiet: healing on every claim would spam join events; heal only when membership is absent AND the tombstone exists. Fourth, file size: claimNextTask.ts is 481 lines, already past moe-next's 400 split threshold -- but moes is not governed by moe-next rails; fix without opportunistic refactoring and note the size rather than absorbing a split this task does not own. Fifth, three of my plans now overlap in this directory -- pathspec commits and the designated merge point (9d5dfec6's eligibility util) are the collision controls; a worker starting this task should check whether 9d5dfec6 landed first and compose with its util instead of adding a parallel predicate. Sixth, the installed-plugin-vs-repo gap: the fleet keeps hitting this bug until the plugin daemon is rebuilt -- the completion note must separate committed from live, and the fleet workaround (join_team + retry once) stays circulated until then. Finally, the corrected moe-next memory file is part of this task's deliverable -- a wrong-cause gotcha is worse than no gotcha, and it must land under this task's id so the correction is attributable.

reviewSummary:
APPROVED on re-review. The rejection's one gap is closed by 9aac506 (test-only, 1 file, +30/-0 — no production byte touched, since the line I flagged was already correct).

THE FIX IS THE KILL I ASKED FOR, re-measured by me: I re-applied the exact mutant that survived the whole package last round — waitForTask.ts's solo filter reverted from `resolveEffectiveTeam(state, workerId)` to `state.getTeamForWorker(workerId)` — and ran `npm test` over the FULL package. Last round: 82 files / 931 tests EXIT=0, mutant invisible. Now: "Tests 1 failed | 931 passed (932)" EXIT=1, and the single failure is the new arm "keeps that evicted member VISIBLE to wait_for_task instead of parking it forever". Restored md5-exact (c5aab6c3…), `git status` clean, `git log -1 -- waitForTask.ts` still 24f13c3 — no production byte moved.

The test is built as the rejection asked: it drives the production waitForTaskTool rather than restating the predicate, asserts hasNext true naming task-free plus timedOut undefined, and pins its own premises first (live membership gone, tombstone present) so it cannot pass for the wrong reason. It also records the read/write asymmetry — wait resolves effective membership but must not rejoin, because a read may not mutate the roster.

GATES re-run at 9aac506: focused `npx vitest run src/tools/claimNextTask.test.ts src/util/teamMembershipHeal.test.ts` -> 2 files / 37 tests EXIT=0 (36 last round, +1); `npx tsc --noEmit` EXIT=0; `npm test` -> 82 files / 932 tests EXIT=0.

Everything approved last round stands and was re-verified green: the NO_TEAM_MEMBERSHIP refusal with its join_team exit, the genuine-race discrimination arm, the tombstone write at both eviction sites, and the leave_team retraction, each previously drilled. The recorded caution (a tombstoned team that has since FILLED UP stays effectively teamed while heal declines the seat) remains deliberately unfixed and non-blocking.
